title: Manowtassquot / Namkee Creek
summary: Manowtassquot and Namkee name creek-boundary geography west of Blue Point. The Namkee entry connects the creek mouth with fishing-place language and a remembered fishing-weir setting.
address_label: General Corey Creek / Namkee Creek boundary area west of Blue Point
map_geometry_source: Approximate modern creek-boundary location west of Blue Point based on Tooker's reading of the Fletcher Patent.
history_content: Boundary creek, Blue Point setting, and fishing-place interpretation are brought together here. Dated documentary context appear in the Historic Timeline.
translation_content:
Manowtassquot is interpreted as a place where flags or rushes were gathered for baskets and mats. Namkee is interpreted as a fishing place or where fish are taken. Recorded forms include Manowtassqtwt, Manowtasquott, Namke, Nanmicuke, Namcuke, Namko, Namkee, and Namkey.

Why Place Names Matter

“Indigenous place names can represent important historical events and legal principles. They can convey teachings on how to live in good relations with others and the land.”

— Yellowhead Institute, Reclaiming Indigenous Place Names: A Policy Brief (2019), PDF page 4

Place-name history should show Native people as active and present, not only as names in old documents.
whereintheworld_content: Sources place Manowtassquot in the creek-boundary area west of Blue Point, often identified with Corey Creek or Namkee Creek. The exact boundary remains uncertain.
